Relevant sentences:
To ensure randomization, intervention and control booklets were placed in a single pile in an order determined by a sequence of random integers generated by a true random number generator (Haahr, 2004). The booklets from this single pile were then distributed in a lecture theatre and laboratory class, and completed under examination conditions.

Analysis:
The text states that intervention and control booklets were randomly ordered in a single pile and distributed to participants. However, it does not provide details on whether the allocation sequence was concealed (e.g., using opaque, sealed envelopes or visually identical covers) to prevent the personnel distributing the booklets or the participants from knowing the assignment prior to enrollment.

REPLY 4 OF 22  label=DII1
==============================================================================
Relevant sentences:
"Participants received a booklet which included: (a) pre-intervention measures, (b) the intervention or control task, and (c) immediate post-intervention measures."
"To reduce the risk of cross condition contamination, participants were explicitly requested not to discuss the contents of their booklet with other participants over the following week."
"The intervention employed persuasive communication targeting self-efficacy and intention, and invited participants to form implementation intentions in relation to acquiring and preparing fruit and vegetables for consumption."
"The control task consisted of questions about the questionnaire itself (e.g. ‘imagine you are talking to a friend about the experience of completing the questionnaire so far. How easy or difficult did you find it?’)."

Analysis:
The trial involved participants completing a booklet containing either a persuasive intervention targeting fruit and vegetable consumption or a control task (questions about the questionnaire). Given the distinct nature of the tasks and the lack of any described blinding mechanism (such as a sham intervention that mimics the persuasive communication), participants were aware of the content and nature of the booklet they completed. Therefore, they were aware of their assigned intervention.

Correct answer:
Yes

"The booklets from this single pile were then distributed in a lecture theatre and laboratory class, and completed under examination conditions. To reduce the risk of cross condition contamination, participants were explicitly requested not to discuss the contents of their booklet with other participants over the following week."

Because the intervention was delivered instantly and participants were instructed not to discuss the booklets, there is no evidence or strong reason to believe that the trial context led to a failure to implement the protocol or to the implementation of non-protocol interventions. There are no indications of deviations from the intended intervention arising from the trial context.

REPLY 9 OF 22  label=DII6
==============================================================================
Relevant sentences: 
"In total, 218 people completed the booklet (115 first-year and 105 second-year students), of whom 15.6% were male and 84.4% were female. At follow-up, 146 people responded; 11.0% were male, and 89.0% were female, with an overall attrition rate of 33%."
"Univariate ANCOVAs showed that three post-intervention behaviour differences were significant when controlling for pre-intervention scores, RDIFV F(1; 143) = 6:83, p , :01; RDIF (i.e. one piece) F(1; 143) = 5:04, p , :05; RDIV (i.e. four portions of vegetables) F(1; 143) = 9:63, p , :01."

Analysis: 
The authors randomized 218 participants, but only 146 provided follow-up data (an attrition rate of 33%). The degrees of freedom in the ANCOVA results (e.g., F(1, 143)) indicate that the analysis was conducted on the subset of participants who provided follow-up data. According to the guidance, a modified intention-to-treat (mITT) analysis that simply excludes participants with missing outcome data is considered an appropriate analysis for estimating the effect of assignment to intervention. 

Correct answer: 
Yes

Relevant sentences:
"In total, 218 people completed the booklet (115 first-year and 105 second-year students), of whom 15.6% were male and 84.4% were female. At follow-up, 146 people responded; 11.0% were male, and 89.0% were female, with an overall attrition rate of 33%."

Analysis:
The text notes an overall attrition rate of 33%, meaning that only the 146 participants who responded at follow-up were analyzed. There is no information provided regarding whether any of the analyzed participants were analyzed in the wrong intervention group, nor is there explicit information confirming that an intention-to-treat analysis was performed on all randomized participants to account for dropouts. Therefore, there is no information to definitively answer whether there was a substantial impact from a failure to analyze participants in the correct groups.

REPLY 11 OF 22  label=MOD1
==============================================================================
Relevant sentences:
"In total, 218 people completed the booklet (115 first-year and 105 second-year students), of whom 15.6% were male and 84.4% were female. At follow-up, 146 people responded; 11.0% were male, and 89.0% were female, with an overall attrition rate of 33%."

Analysis:
The text clearly states that out of the 218 participants who initially completed the booklet, only 146 responded at follow-up. This resulted in an overall attrition rate of 33%. Since "nearly all" typically requires data availability from 95% of the participants for continuous outcomes, a 33% loss to follow-up indicates that data were not available for all or nearly all randomized participants.

REPLY 12 OF 22  label=MOD2
==============================================================================
Relevant sentences:
At follow-up, 146 people responded; 11.0% were male, and 89.0% were female, with an overall attrition rate of 33%.
However, a MANOVA performed on study variables by drop-out status indicated a significant omnibus difference, F(8; 209) = 2.05, p < .05, and subsequent ANOVAs revealed that, disregarding experimental condition, participants who completed the follow-up questionnaire reported significantly higher pre-intervention intentions, anticipated regret, and fruit and vegetable consumption.
Moreover, a MANOVA detected a significant difference between those who did and those who did not complete the follow-up questionnaire.

Analysis:
The trial experienced an overall attrition rate of 33%. The authors conducted analyses comparing completers with dropouts and found significant differences in pre-intervention characteristics (intentions, anticipated regret, and baseline fruit and vegetable consumption). However, the study does not report using any analysis methods designed to correct for bias due to missing outcome data (such as multiple imputation or inverse probability weighting), nor does it present sensitivity analyses demonstrating that the results are robust under various plausible assumptions about the missing data. 

Correct answer:
No

REPLY 13 OF 22  label=MOD3
==============================================================================
Relevant sentences:
"At follow-up, 146 people responded; 11.0% were male, and 89.0% were female, with an overall attrition rate of 33%."
"However, a MANOVA performed on study variables by drop-out status indicated a significant omnibus difference, F(8; 209) ¼ 2:05, p , :05, and subsequent ANOVAs revealed that, disregarding experimental condition, participants who completed the follow-up questionnaire reported significantly higher pre-intervention intentions, anticipated regret, and fruit and vegetable consumption."

Analysis:
The article states that there was an overall attrition rate of 33%. Furthermore, analyses comparing drop-outs to completers showed that those who completed the follow-up had significantly higher baseline fruit and vegetable consumption, intentions, and anticipated regret compared to those who dropped out. Since baseline consumption is strongly related to the outcome (follow-up consumption), and those with lower baseline consumption were more likely to have missing outcome data, it is likely that the missingness in the outcome depended on its true value (i.e., those who consumed less were more likely to drop out).

Correct answer:
Probably yes
==============================================================================
REPLY 14 OF 22  label=MOD4
==============================================================================
Relevant sentences:
"An ANOVA performed on age, F(1, 141) = .03, ns, and chi-squared tests on gender, x2(1) = 1.26, ns, and drop-out rate by condition, x2(1) = 1.77, ns, revealed no significant differences, suggesting that randomization was successful."
"However, a MANOVA performed on study variables by drop-out status indicated a significant omnibus difference, F(8, 209) = 2.05, p < .05, and subsequent ANOVAs revealed that, disregarding experimental condition, participants who completed the follow-up questionnaire reported significantly higher pre-intervention intentions, anticipated regret, and fruit and vegetable consumption."

Analysis:
The text states that the drop-out rate did not differ significantly between the intervention and control conditions. While those who dropped out had lower baseline intentions and fruit/vegetable consumption compared to those who stayed, this was true across both conditions ("disregarding experimental condition"). Because the proportions of missing data do not differ significantly between the intervention groups, and there is no reported evidence that the reasons for missing data differ between groups or are directly tied to the true unobserved outcome values in a way that introduces bias between groups, it is not likely that missingness in the outcome depended on its true value in a problematic manner.

Correct answer:
Probably no

REPLY 15 OF 22  label=MO1
==============================================================================
Relevant sentences:
Behaviour related to consuming the RDIFV was measured by three items: (a) ‘on how many days did you eat at least one piece of fruit over the last week? (write in the number of days)’; (b) ‘on how many days didyoueat four or more serving spoons of vegetables (100% of the vegetables for the RDIFV) over the last week? (write in the number of days)’; and (c) ‘on how many days did you eat the RDIFV (four serving spoons of vegetables and one piece of fruit) over the last week? (write in the number of days)’. These items were completed immediately prior to the intervention and at follow-up 1 week later.

Analysis:
The outcome (fruit and vegetable consumption) was measured using self-reported items asking participants about their intake over the previous week. While self-report measures can be subject to recall bias, they are standard and widely used methods for assessing dietary behaviors over short timeframes. There is no indication that this measurement method is unlikely to be sensitive to plausible intervention effects or that it has been demonstrated to have poor validity for this specific purpose. Thus, the method of measuring the outcome is considered appropriate.

Correct answer:
Probably no

"A controlled, pre- post-test experimental study with random allocation and a 1 week self-report behavioural follow-up was conducted."
"Follow-up behavioural measures were administered in the same context 1 week later."
"Behaviour related to consuming the RDIFV was measured by three items... These items were completed immediately prior to the intervention and at follow-up 1 week later."

Analysis:
The context indicates that the outcomes were measured using the same self-report items for both the intervention and control groups, and these measures were administered in the same context 1 week after the intervention. Because the same data collection methods and time points were used for all participants regardless of their assigned group, the measurement or ascertainment of the outcome did not differ between the intervention groups.

Relevant sentences:
"A controlled, pre- post-test experimental study with random allocation and a 1 week self-report behavioural follow-up was conducted."
"Participants received a booklet which included: (a) pre-intervention measures, (b) the intervention or control task, and (c) immediate post-intervention measures."

Since the intervention consisted of receiving and completing an intervention or control booklet (a brief leaflet-like intervention), it is highly likely that the participants (and thus the outcome assessors) were aware of the intervention they received.

REPLY 18 OF 22  label=MO4
==============================================================================
**Relevant sentences:**
"A controlled, pre- post-test experimental study with random allocation and a 1 week self-report behavioural follow-up was conducted." 
"Behaviour related to consuming the RDIFV was measured by three items: (a) ‘on how many days did you eat at least one piece of fruit over the last week? (write in the number of days)’; (b) ‘on how many days didyoueat four or more serving spoons of vegetables (100% of the vegetables for the RDIFV) over the last week? (write in the number of days)’; and (c) ‘on how many days did you eat the RDIFV (four serving spoons of vegetables and one piece of fruit) over the last week? (write in the number of days)’."

**Analysis:**
The outcome is the amount of fruit and vegetables consumed, which was measured entirely via participant self-report. Because the intervention was behavioral (completing a leaflet with persuasive messages and planning tasks), participants were aware of the intervention they received. As the participants were effectively the outcome assessors for their own behavior, and the outcome is a subjective self-report measure, their knowledge of the assigned intervention could easily have influenced their assessment of the outcome.

**Correct answer:**
Yes

REPLY 19 OF 22  label=MO5
==============================================================================
**Relevant sentences:**
"Behaviour related to consuming the RDIFV was measured by three items: (a) ‘on how many days did you eat at least one piece of fruit over the last week? (write in the number of days)’; (b) ‘on how many days did you eat four or more serving spoons of vegetables (100% of the vegetables for the RDIFV) over the last week? (write in the number of days)’; and (c) ‘on how many days did you eat the RDIFV (four serving spoons of vegetables and one piece of fruit) over the last week? (write in the number of days)’."
"These items were completed immediately prior to the intervention and at follow-up 1 week later."
"Third, we were limited to self-report measures of behaviour..."

**Analysis:**
The primary outcome of the study (fruit and vegetable consumption) was assessed using self-reported measures where participants recorded the number of days they achieved dietary targets over the past week. Because the participants were not blinded to the intervention—which consisted of persuasive communication and planning exercises specifically designed to increase fruit and vegetable intake—they were fully aware of their intervention status. Given the subjective nature of self-reported dietary habits and the clear behavioral goals of the intervention, it is highly possible that social desirability or expectancy biases influenced how participants estimated and reported their own consumption at the 1-week follow-up. Therefore, it is likely that the assessment of the outcome was influenced by knowledge of the intervention received.

**Correct answer:**
Probably yes
